title: RED Interview · Knowledge base
description: Source-based English study collection on audio, torrents, spectra, ripping and rules. A study aid, no guarantee of full mastery.

collectionFormat.optional: image is a relative asset path; sourceParagraphs and evidence are coverage metadata
collectionFormat.install: Copy knowledge.json into a knowledge/ directory; application loads the file as JSON

questions.question: What characterises an analog music source?

answers.text: It is already a binary file
A physical medium was altered and must be digitised via an ADC
It necessarily comes from a CD

questions.explanation: Analog media store music through physical alterations; turning it into a file requires analog-to-digital conversion.

questions.question: Which statement about vinyl and cassettes matches the source?

answers.text: Vinyl is allowed; cassettes only under strict conditions

questions.explanation: The source states vinyl is always allowed, but cassettes only under strict conditions.

questions.question: What is a digital source?

answers.text: A medium that stores music as binary data
A tape with a stronger magnetic field

questions.explanation: CD, DVD, SACD and purchased web downloads are examples of digital sources.

questions.question: What does “web rip” mean in the source?

answers.text: Any download from an artist page
A lossy transcode of an audio stream
A CD rip in the browser

questions.explanation: A web rip is explicitly a lossy transcode of a stream; a web download is distinct from it.

questions.question: Which three classes does the source name?
questions.explanation: The classification is uncompressed lossless, compressed lossless and lossy.

questions.question: What does a higher bitrate mean when comparing the same recording?

answers.text: More bits per unit of time; for the same music, generally higher quality

questions.explanation: Bitrate is given in kbps; for the same music, the higher bitrate is higher quality.

questions.question: Which pair is uncompressed lossless (PCM)?
questions.explanation: WAV and AIFF are given as PCM examples.

questions.question: Which statement about lossless transcoding is correct?

answers.text: Lossless formats preserve all original data and can be converted between each other without quality loss
Lossless is always smaller than lossy

questions.explanation: Compressed and uncompressed lossless formats retain all data.

questions.question: What does a lossy format typically remove?

answers.text: Some original data, often in high frequencies

questions.explanation: Lossy files are smaller because original data is removed; the source warns of audible differences.

questions.question: Which lossy format is permitted on RED at minimum as MP3?
questions.explanation: The stated minimum is 192 kbps CBR or V2 VBR.

questions.question: Which statement about AAC does the source make?

answers.text: AAC is allowed but can be trumped by any MP3 torrent, except iTunes purchases with exclusive tracks

questions.explanation: The iTunes exception is explicitly named.

questions.question: Which sizes does the example for Sk8er Boi (3:24) give?

answers.text: WAV 34.3 MB; FLAC 25.75 MB; MP3 320 CBR 7.78 MB
WAV 7.78 MB; FLAC 34.3 MB; MP3 25.75 MB

questions.explanation: These are the concrete comparison values from the source.

questions.question: What does transparency mean?

answers.text: Through normal listening without prior knowledge, the average person cannot tell lossy and lossless apart

questions.explanation: The source calls MP3 192 CBR transparent for most people; this is a listening definition, not proof of authenticity.

questions.question: What does LAME stand for in the source?

answers.text: LAME Ain’t An MP3 Encoder; an open-source MP3 encoder

questions.explanation: LAME is a customisable open-source encoder for MP3.

questions.question: What is typical of CBR?

answers.text: Bitrate varies and file size is unpredictable
Constant target bitrate per second and a predictable file size

questions.explanation: CBR allocates the same number of bits per second regardless of complexity.

questions.question: What do you control with VBR?

answers.text: A target quality; the bitrate varies with complexity

questions.explanation: VBR targets quality; the average is derived from file size and duration.

questions.question: Which mapping is correct?
questions.explanation: V0 is the highest and V9 the lowest VBR preset; V2 is the RED minimum quality.

questions.question: Which ranges does the source give approximately for V0 and V2?
questions.explanation: These are the stated typical average bitrate ranges.

questions.question: What is ABR?

answers.text: Variable bitrate without a target value
Variable distribution with a set average; per the source, not recommended

questions.explanation: ABR combines a CBR target average with variable distribution but is not recommended.

questions.question: What is a good transcode?

answers.text: Never lossy, or lossy only once as the final step

questions.explanation: Lossless↔lossless is harmless; lossless→lossy once as the final step stays good.

questions.question: Which chain is bad according to the source?
questions.explanation: Lossy→lossless is a forbidden bad transcode.

questions.question: What is a peer?

answers.text: Someone who has added the same torrent

questions.explanation: Peers share data in the same torrent swarm.

questions.question: When do you earn upload credit?

answers.text: As soon as you merely seed
When another peer downloads from you; merely seeding is not enough

questions.explanation: The source distinguishes seeding availability from data actually transferred.

questions.question: How is the ratio calculated?

answers.text: Seed time divided by file size

questions.explanation: Amount uploaded divided by amount downloaded.

questions.question: What does neutral leech mean?
questions.explanation: With neutral leech, neither data amount is counted as usual.

questions.question: What applies to a freeleech token?

answers.text: It applies to all users and without limit
Download doesn’t count for you; up to 5 GB and until the download finishes or 7 days

questions.explanation: The source names both limits: 5 GB plus end of download or seven days.

questions.question: What happens if you fall below the required ratio?

answers.text: Two weeks of ratio watch; afterwards possibly disabled downloads

questions.explanation: Improvement is possible through seeding, requests or rule-compliant uploads.

questions.question: What does port forwarding do?

answers.text: It forwards a port through NAT to the client and improves connectability

questions.explanation: Direct connections can increase upload opportunities.

questions.question: What is a partial seeder?

answers.text: A peer with the whole torrent
A peer who seeds only part and doesn’t want to download the rest

questions.explanation: The source warns against downloading large examples just to boost ratio.

questions.question: What must be set when uploading a private torrent?
questions.explanation: The private marking keeps non-members out of the peer list.

questions.question: What does a spectrogram show?
questions.explanation: Frequency against time; Hz and kHz measure frequencies.

questions.question: Which statement is methodologically correct?

answers.text: A cutoff alone proves codec and authenticity
Spectra help with transcode checks, but a spectrum alone proves no codec or authenticity

questions.explanation: The source uses spectra as an aid; genres also look different. The quiz avoids treating it as sole proof.

questions.question: Which cutoff is given for MP3 320 CBR?
questions.explanation: The source gives approximately 20.5 kHz.

questions.question: Which cutoff is given for MP3 V2?
questions.explanation: V2 is given as roughly 18.5 kHz.

questions.question: What can a FLAC spectrum with an MP3-192 cutoff indicate?
questions.explanation: The source shows exactly this example as a bad MP3-192→FLAC transcode.

questions.question: Which tools are recommended?
questions.explanation: Audition, Audacity and SoX are used for spectral analysis; MediaInfo etc. help with the claimed bitrate value.

questions.question: What is a log?

answers.text: Text file with the ripping process and errors

questions.explanation: The .log file documents the entire ripping process.

questions.question: May a log be modified?

answers.text: No; it can trigger warnings and loss of privileges

questions.explanation: The source forbids any modification.

questions.question: What is a CUE file for?

answers.text: It catalogues a CD and enables identical burning

questions.explanation: CUE is the table of contents/TOC of the CD.

questions.question: Which programs are suggested?
questions.explanation: EAC for Windows/Linux with Wine, XLD for macOS.

questions.question: What is allowed regarding accounts?
questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: May you trade accounts or invitations?

answers.text: Trading, selling or publicly giving away accounts/invitations is forbidden

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What are you responsible for regarding invitations?

answers.text: For the invitees’ compliance with the rules, especially the Golden Rules

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What is ratio manipulation?

answers.text: Increasing buffer through unintended use of protocol/features

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What is cheating?

answers.text: Reporting false tracker data, including via a modified client

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: Which clients are allowed?

answers.text: Only whitelisted clients without modification; new unstable clients only with staff approval

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What applies to .torrent files?

answers.text: Do not modify, share, or disclose the passkey

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: How should you handle private user data?

answers.text: Do not blackmail, threaten, expose or harvest personal data
A Google search is enough as permission

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: How are staff decisions contested?

answers.text: Resolve it privately with the deciding moderator/staff, no moderator shopping

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What is backseat moderation?

answers.text: Confronting users over suspected violations; report instead

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What applies to special events?

answers.text: Staff decides; users may not demand them

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: How may automated access occur?

answers.text: Via the API, at most 5 requests per 10 seconds

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What is forbidden with freeleech autosnatching?

answers.text: Automatic snatching with little/no user input

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What applies to Tor?

answers.text: Browsing and torrenting via Tor is forbidden; non-Tor VPNs only under the stated safeguards

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What should you do about bugs?

answers.text: Report critical bugs responsibly; do not exploit or publish exploits

questions.explanation: This rule is set out in the “Golden Rules” section of the source.

questions.question: What makes something a dupe?

answers.text: Same music with comparable format/bitrate/sampling; different content may coexist

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: When can an inactive torrent be replaced?

answers.text: After two weeks without a seed, by an identical reseed or a new rip/encode

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: What does trumping mean?

answers.text: Replacing a non-compliant torrent in a rule-compliant way

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: Which lossy uploads are especially durable?

answers.text: MP3 V0 or 320 CBR, always, despite a dupe
MP3 V0 or 320 CBR, provided no identical rip exists

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: Which four tag fields are required?
questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: What may a music torrent not contain?

answers.text: Archives such as RAR, ZIP, TAR or ISO containing music

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: How do you name a good folder?

answers.text: Meaningful: Artist - Album (Year) - Format; no unnecessary nested folders

questions.explanation: This rule is in the “Dupes/Trumps” section of the source.

questions.question: Which chain describes the cassette case?

answers.text: Tape magnetisation → tape deck → recorder/ADC → digital file

questions.explanation: The source describes magnetising the tape and digitising it via a recorder.

questions.question: Which examples does the source name for digital sources?

answers.text: CDs, DVDs, SACDs and web downloads

questions.explanation: These four source types are explicitly named.

questions.question: Why are uncompressed lossless files especially large?

answers.text: Silence gets the same amount of bits per second as sound

questions.explanation: With PCM, even silence gets the same bitrate.

questions.question: Which statement about lossy→lossy and lossy→lossless is correct?

answers.text: Both work without further quality loss
Lossy cannot be converted to another lossy without further loss, nor to genuine lossless

questions.explanation: The source stresses that a lossy source cannot make the file genuinely lossless again.

questions.question: Which formats does the source name as lossy examples?

answers.text: MP3, AAC, WMA, AC3 and DTS

questions.explanation: All five are in the lossy list.

questions.question: Which formats are allowed on RED as a lossless upload?
questions.explanation: The upload rule restricts lossless to FLAC.

questions.question: Why are iTunes AAC exceptions provided for?

answers.text: Because of iTunes-specific bonus/exclusive tracks and because AAC cannot be losslessly converted back

questions.explanation: The source names iTunes exclusive tracks as the exception.

questions.question: Which two factors determine the resulting file size with VBR?

answers.text: The preset and the required music data

questions.explanation: Preset quality and complexity/music data determine the size.

questions.question: How is the average VBR bitrate value explained?

answers.text: Number of tracks divided by size

questions.explanation: The source describes the average as size divided by duration.

questions.question: Which chain is a good transcode according to the source?
questions.explanation: Lossless-to-lossless preserves the data; repeated lossy conversion is bad.

questions.question: Which chain is explicitly forbidden?

answers.text: Uncompressed lossless → lossy as the final step

questions.explanation: Lossy to lossless is a bad transcode and forbidden on RED.

questions.question: When is upload credit created?

answers.text: When another peer leeched from you and data was transferred

questions.explanation: Merely seeding gives no upload credit; a transfer to a leecher does.

questions.question: What counts when the same torrent is downloaded twice?
questions.explanation: The source states explicitly that downloading twice counts twice.

questions.question: Which combination describes a freeleech token?

answers.text: Download doesn’t count toward your ratio; up to 5 GB; until completion or 7 days
Upload and download never count; unlimited

questions.explanation: These are the three stated restrictions/effects.

questions.question: What does neutral leech mean?

answers.text: No upload or download data counts toward the ratio

questions.explanation: Neutral leech, per the source, counts neither data amount.

questions.question: What does port forwarding do?

answers.text: Direct public connections to the client are made easier and upload opportunities rise
It sets the ratio to zero

questions.explanation: Forwarded ports increase connectability.

questions.question: Why are Rosetta Stone and 30-CD Mozart torrents unsuitable as a ratio strategy?

answers.text: Because of many partial seeders who seed only parts
Because they may have no peers
Because they exist only as MP3

questions.explanation: The source names these huge torrents as typical partial-seeder traps.

questions.question: What must be enabled when creating a private RED torrent?
questions.explanation: The private flag keeps non-members out of the peer list.

questions.question: Which cutoff belongs to MP3 192 CBR?
questions.explanation: The source gives 19 kHz for 192 CBR.

questions.question: Which cutoff belongs to MP3 V2?
questions.explanation: The source gives 18.5 kHz for V2.

questions.question: Which cutoff belongs to MP3 128 CBR?
questions.explanation: The source gives 16 kHz for 128 CBR.

questions.question: Why is the .flac extension not enough to prove authenticity?

answers.text: A FLAC can be transcoded from MP3; a spectral check is necessary

questions.explanation: The 21.8 MB example shows a file named FLAC but created from MP3 192 — a lossy→lossless case.

questions.question: Which combination does the source name for detection and the subsequent spectral check?

answers.text: Audio Identifier/dBpoweramp or dnuos/MediaInfo for the claimed bitrate; Audition/Audacity/SoX for the spectral check

questions.explanation: Determine metadata/encoding first, then check the spectral view with the recommended programs.

questions.question: What must not happen to a log file?

answers.text: It must not be modified for any reason
It must be renamed to MP3

questions.explanation: Manipulation leads, per the source, to warnings up to account suspension.

questions.question: What is a CUE file for?

answers.text: As a table of contents/TOC for burning an identical CD

questions.explanation: CUE catalogues the CD and enables identical burning.

questions.question: Which programs does the source recommend?

answers.text: EAC for Windows/Linux with Wine and XLD for macOS

questions.explanation: EAC and XLD produce high-quality rips with sufficient logs.

questions.question: How many accounts are allowed per user?
questions.explanation: Additional accounts are not allowed under any circumstances; if deactivated, contact staff.

questions.question: What happens to an account you no longer want?

answers.text: Staff PM for deactivation; accounts are not deleted

questions.explanation: The source says explicitly: request deactivation, do not delete.

questions.question: Which invite action is forbidden?

answers.text: Offering publicly or on public invite giveaway/trading sites
Responding to an offer in the Invites forum

questions.explanation: Public offers and responses to public requests are forbidden.

questions.question: When may you request an invite in the Invites forum?

answers.text: As a Power User or higher, and only when an offer exists

questions.explanation: Requests there are restricted to Power User+ and only by message when an offer exists.

questions.question: What is ratio manipulation?

answers.text: Transferring/increasing buffer through unintended protocol/site use, e.g. request abuse

questions.explanation: The source names transferring/increasing buffer through unintended uses.

questions.question: Which client rule applies?

answers.text: Only whitelisted clients; no modified clients; unstable tests need staff approval

questions.explanation: The client whitelist and the modification ban are explicit.

questions.question: Why may RED .torrent files not be modified?

answers.text: Non-RED announce URLs could report false data and count as cheating

questions.explanation: Embedding foreign announce URLs is prohibited.

questions.question: What does the personal passkey in the .torrent protect?

answers.text: It lets the tracker attribute statistics; do not share the file/passkey

questions.explanation: Passkeys are personal and must not be shared.

questions.question: Which use of Tor is allowed?

answers.text: None: browsing and torrenting over Tor are forbidden; non-Tor VPNs may be used under conditions

questions.explanation: The source forbids Tor; VPN/proxy/seedbox is possible with 2FA or up to 3 IP whitelist entries.

questions.question: How is automated access regulated?

answers.text: API only; at most 5 requests in 10 seconds; no HTML scraping

questions.explanation: These are the concrete API limits.

questions.question: What applies to freeleech autosnatching?

answers.text: It is forbidden if automated with little/no user intervention
It is only allowed via HTML

questions.explanation: API, log or site-scraping automation is explicitly named.

questions.question: What should you do with a critical bug?

answers.text: Report it immediately under the responsible-disclosure rule; do not exploit it
Sell it in the Invites forum

questions.explanation: Searching for and exploiting live bugs is forbidden; report critical bugs immediately.

questions.question: What defines a distinct edition more than catalogue data does?

answers.text: Rip log TOC, peak level, pregaps, tracklist and order

questions.explanation: Catalogue number/packaging alone is not enough; year and label can distinguish releases.

questions.question: When may an inactive torrent be trumped?

answers.text: After two weeks without a seeder; reseed the original file if possible

questions.explanation: After two weeks of inactivity, a reseed or a new rip/encode is possible; prefer the original file.

questions.question: Which log hierarchy is correct?

answers.text: A FLAC without a suitable log can be trumped by an approved-tool log; 100% beats a lower score

questions.explanation: The source distinguishes missing/unapproved logs and scores; a lower score may not trump an existing lower score.

questions.question: Which four tag fields are required?
questions.explanation: These four fields are named by the tag-trump rule.

questions.question: Which tag change is not enough for a trump according to the source?

answers.text: Only adding diacritics, fixing minor typos or adding an alternative spelling
Fully completing a missing title field

questions.explanation: Minor improvements do not count as a substantial improvement.

questions.question: What is the minimum requirement for a music folder?

answers.text: It contains the album name and the music; single tracks also sit in a torrent folder
Music may sit in a RAR

questions.explanation: Archives are forbidden; even a single file needs the folder.

questions.question: Which folder structure is explicitly not allowed?

answers.text: One folder for Disc 1 and one for Disc 2

questions.explanation: Nested folders such as an extra album folder are not allowed.

questions.question: How do you resolve identical track numbers for multiple discs in one folder?

answers.text: Put discs in separate folders or prefix disc numbers, e.g. 1-01

questions.explanation: Both options are in the source.

questions.question: Which statement describes the format hierarchy as a rule, without copying the image captions?

answers.text: Higher/more robust formats cannot be trumped; weaker allowed lossy uploads can be replaced by better ones, but lossy must never be up-transcoded to FLAC/320/V0
Any lossy file may be uploaded as FLAC

questions.explanation: The hierarchy serves as a decision rule; no transcoding for supposed improvement.
